detail:
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) reports that its Obstructive Lung Diseases Branch oversees much of the asthma research it supports, through an Asthma Program focused on how external triggers, genetics, and risk factors contribute to abnormal lung inflammation. The program also studies novel therapeutic approaches for clinical management of asthma in adults and children, including more precise, individualized treatment approaches for people whose asthma responds differently to particular therapies.

Current research areas described by NHLBI include new approaches to improve treatment options for severe asthma, studies of asthma biology such as the bacteria present in the airways, and research on disparities, including work on genetic risk in populations of African ancestry and a program studying differences in heart and lung disease across groups. NHLBI presents these projects as ongoing funded research, and investigational approaches in the sources remain in study rather than established treatment.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about asthma research and clinical trials.
sourceName: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
summary: NHLBI describes its asthma research program as studying triggers, genetics, and inflammation, alongside new and more personalized treatment approaches for severe asthma, asthma biology, and disparities between groups.
takeaways: research focuses on triggers, genetics, and lung inflammation
severe asthma and personalized treatment are active study areas
investigational approaches remain in trials, not established care
title: Asthma: research into triggers, biology, and personalized treatment
